title: K-th Digit in Infinite String
summary: Given an integer k, construct an infinite string by concatenating the decimal representations of positive integers in a specific order.
statement: Given an integer k, construct an infinite string by concatenating the decimal representations of positive integers in a specific order. For each block b, integers from 10*b to 10*b+9 are appended. If b is even, integers are added in increasing order; if b is odd, in decreasing order. Return the k-th digit of this string, indexed starting at 1.
constraints: The infinite string begins with 1 through 9.
Then each block b contributes ten consecutive integers 10b..10b+9, ascending for even b and descending for odd b.
hints: Subtract complete groups sharing the same integer digit width.
Each block has ten integers and group sizes grow by powers of ten.
Locate the block, number offset, and digit offset with division and remainders.
Parity determines whether the number offset counts upward or downward.
editorial: Parity determines whether the number offset counts upward or downward.

tests.explanation: The fourth digit of the initial 123456789 prefix is four.
Block one is descending, so the tenth digit is the first digit of nineteen: one.
